title: The Daily echopoint monitor ran two security flows from stale published versions
service: echopoint flow suites (prod CI org, monitor `Daily echopoint`), echopoint flow versions
summary: At 09:00Z the `Daily echopoint` monitor failed two flows: `security — auth forgery & scheme boundaries` expected `BAD_REQUEST` and `security — ephemeral direct completion contract` expected `200`. Both had been updated to the echopoint#733 contract on 2026-11-04, and the gate and suite runs passed on them. A monitor runs a flow's latest **published** version, while `flows run` (suites and gate) runs the draft; these flows had versions published on 2026-10-17/20, and the 2026-11-04 updates were never published. Four flows had this drift. The routine published all four at 12:13Z and added a drift check to the suite script. Dev and CI only: the monitor calls the dev APIs and no deploy was held.

impact.text: Two red flows in the Daily monitor run on dev, a failure email to the monitor owner, and a monitor that tested a contract echopoint replaced on 2026-11-03. No prod deploy was held: the gate runs the drafts.

trigger: The `Daily echopoint` monitor ran at 2026-11-05T09:00:04Z, the first run since 2026-11-01, and launched the latest published version of each selected flow.
detection: The routine read the monitor's scheduled executions at about 12:11Z while it checked that echopoint#742 had unblocked the Daily monitor. The monitor also emailed its owner on failure; nothing reads that email automatically.
resolution: `flows publish` on the four drifted flows at 12:13:10Z. A rescan at 12:14:41Z found no flow whose draft differs from its latest published version. The drafts are green in the suites and the gate, so the next Daily run uses green definitions.

whys.problem: The Daily echopoint monitor failed two flows on behaviour echopoint changed on purpose two days earlier

because.text: The monitor ran versions of the flows published on 2026-10-17/20, not the updated definitions
because.evidence: Scheduled runs asserted `200` and `BAD_REQUEST`; only the published versions hold those values (`flows version list` diff)

because.text: A monitor launches a flow's latest published version, and a flow run from the CLI or gate launches the draft
because.evidence: `flowschedules/service.go:521` `latestPublishedVersionID`; `flows launch` and `flows run` take no version

because.text: The 2026-11-04 updates changed only the drafts; nobody published them
The fix procedure (update the gate flow, run it, see green) checks only the draft path
because.evidence: Workspace AGENTS.md cross-repo rule and skills `flow-suite-testing` named no publish step

because.text: Nothing compares a flow's draft with its published version, so a suite or gate pass says nothing about what monitors run
`flows update` accepts a change to a flow with published versions without a word
because.evidence: echopoint-cli `flows update` output: no warning about published versions

because.text: The flow API and CLI do not tell an editor that monitors keep running an older published version
The failure stayed unseen for three hours and the drift for a day
The Daily monitor did not run from 2026-11-01 to 2026-11-05, so no earlier run showed the drift
because.evidence: No scheduled executions of `1d02b3cf` before 2026-11-05T09:00Z since 2026-11-01; echopoint#742

because.text: A fan-out settle bug kept scheduled runs from finishing, so the monitor skipped every day (fixed by echopoint#742)
A failed monitor run only emails the monitor owner; the routine reads gate runs, not monitor runs
because.evidence: Monitor `recipient_emails` = owner only; Run notes checked Deploy Router gates only

because.text: The routine had no step that lists failed scheduled runs in the suite org

contributing: The two other drifted flows (F-3, F-5) passed: their drafts differ only by the workspace header, and their published assertions already expected the fixed contract.
Most suite flows have no published version, so the monitor runs their drafts; the four tracker flows were the exception.

well: The monitor's per-flow error message named the expected and actual values, so the stale version was found in two queries.
The flow version API keeps every published definition, so the diff proved the cause.
wrong: Three sessions updated these flows on 2026-11-04 and none checked whether they had published versions.
The routine's Run notes described the monitor as a runner of tags, not of published versions.
lucky: The gate runs drafts. Had the gate run published versions, the #733 fix would have held echopoint prod.
The drift hit a dev-only CI monitor. A customer's monitor or a public status page flow with a stale published version would report a false outage.

actions.what: Publish the four drifted flows and rescan for drift
`run_suites.sh` prints `PUBLISH-DRIFT` for each tag flow whose draft differs from its latest published version
`flow-suite-testing` skill: find which version each caller runs; publish after updating a published flow
echopoint-cli `flows update` (and the flow editor) warn when the flow has a published version that monitors keep running
`run_suites.sh` prints `MONITOR-FAILED` for every failed scheduled run in the last 24 h; the routine triages each
Settle schedule runs whose executions are no longer visible (echopoint#742)

messaging.internal: The Daily echopoint monitor failed two security flows at 09:00Z because monitors run the latest published flow version and the 2026-11-04 fixes changed only drafts. Published; the suite script now flags draft/published drift.
